obligations.note: The change adds `coapplicant_tax_id`, a tax identifier and so NPI by ENC-1's own definition, to `ApplicantFields.ALL`. It is not added to `NpiRegistry.FIELDS` or to `mortgage.npi_fields` in policy-params, so it would be persisted unsealed. The exhaustive EncryptionControlTest only enumerates the registry, so its pass does not cover the new field.

`Retention.purge` now removes `coapplicant_tax_id` explicitly, and the hold and cutoff logic is unchanged. However, the only control test, `sampledPurgeRespectsHold`, is sample coverage against an exhaustive requirement, and the CI reports themselves are not valid evidence (see CHG-4).

The new tax-id field is outside the NPI registry, so masking and redaction keyed on the registry may not treat it as NPI. The only evidence is a sample control test, and the fixtures were changed to include the field. Whether it can reach logs unmasked cannot be established.

Ticket CHG-25867 was approved by change manager Erik Brandt on 2026-10-11, before review. Its components (`mortgage.cases`, `mortgage.retention`, `mortgage.control-tests`) cover all three touched paths.
Wen Li, a `change_approver` for baseline-mortgage and not the author Priya Raman under any of her addresses, approved `code_review` on the head commit.
Both approvals name the single head commit 56dda280, so no later commits exist.

`run.json` names the head commit on ci-runner-07 (started 2026-10-13), but the JUnit reports carry timestamp 2026-10-23 and host `dev-laptop-7.local`. That is after the review time (2026-10-16) and is a local machine, not the CI run. The reports are not valid evidence of this run's test results.
The touched components (`mortgage.cases`, `mortgage.retention`, `mortgage.control-tests`) are not marked `security_sensitive`, so no `security_review` approval is required.
`ControlFixtures.java` is under the protected path `src/test/java/controls/*`. Rachel Stein (`control_owner`, controls-office, outside the author's lending-eng team) approved the head commit.
No exception in the register covers ENC-1 for mortgage components. The unsealed-NPI deviation therefore has no approved, unexpired, in-scope exception.
The ledger entries cover `Approvals`, `Policy`, `Underwriting` and payments symbols, none of which this change alters. No accepted evidence lapses.

summary: The change introduces a co-applicant tax identifier, which is NPI, as an ordinary applicant field without registering it in `NpiRegistry`. It would therefore be stored unsealed, violating ENC-1. The explicit purge in `Retention` shows the author treated it as NPI while bypassing the registry, and no exception covers the deviation. In addition, the attached JUnit reports postdate the review time and come from a local workstation rather than the recorded CI run, so they cannot evidence CHG-4. The change is rejected.
